summary: Configured node1 as the cluster's internal chrony time server and node2 as its client via an Ansible playbook run from node3 (the Ansible-equipped control node). Fixed missing SSH host keys/sshd on node1 and node2 to enable Ansible connectivity, then applied /root/ansible-timesync/playbook.yml against inventory.ini. Verified node2 tracks node1 (not a public server) as its current best source. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes with boot_id proof of restart and post-restart health/recovery verification.
actions_performed: Inspected all 3 nodes: identified node3 as the Ansible-equipped control node (Ubuntu 24.04 everywhere)
Fixed missing SSH host keys and inactive sshd service on node1 and node2 (ssh-keygen -A + systemctl enable --now ssh)
Authorized CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY for root on node1 and node2
Wrote Ansible inventory (time_server=node1, time_client=node2) and playbook.yml on node3 at /root/ansible-timesync/

Playbook: installs chrony, configures node1 as chrony server (allow 10.100.123.0/24, local stratum 10 fallback), configures node2 with 'server 10.100.123.10 iburst prefer' replacing default public pool
Ran ansible-playbook successfully against both hosts (using root + id_ed25519 since project-default ansible_user 'antrieb' does not exist on these nodes)

Verified node1 chronyd listening on UDP 123 and synced to public upstream; verified node2's chronyc sources shows node1 (vm-rhel7-2772538802 / 10.100.123.10) as the '*' current best source via chronyc waitsync
Captured boot_id + service-health baseline on all 3 nodes

Restarted node1, node2, node3 one at a time via background 'reboot', polled until exec succeeded again, and confirmed changed boot_id plus recovered chrony health (node1 serving, node2 re-synced to node1) and intact ansible artifacts on node3

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as internal chrony time source for the cluster
evidence.summary: Playbook run shows chrony installed/configured/restarted on node1 (ok=5 changed=3); chronyc tracking + sources -v + ss -ulnp show chronyd active, stratum 10 fallback, listening on UDP 123, synced to public upstreams to redistribute time internally

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to sync against node1 instead of a public time server
evidence.summary: Playbook wrote 'server 10.100.123.10 iburst prefer' as node2's only NTP source; chronyc waitsync + tracking + sources -v on node2 show Reference ID 0A647B0A (10.100.123.10) marked '*' as the current best/synchronized source, stratum 11 (one above node1's 10)
Inventory and playbook created on the ansible-equipped node3; ansible-playbook executed both plays (time_server, time_client) successfully with 0 failures/unreachable
Baseline boot_id b19a635d...; reboot triggered; reconnection after timeout shows new boot_id 18f755e5... (changed); post-restart chrony is active+enabled, listening on UDP 123, synced to upstream

evidence.requirement: node2 restart persistence and re-sync to node1
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 17b362d1...; reboot triggered; new boot_id 2c4063e6... after reconnect (changed); chronyc waitsync confirms chrony active+enabled and re-synchronized to node1 (Reference ID 0A647B0A) post-restart
Baseline boot_id c030bd0d...; reboot triggered; new boot_id dfcd38c9... after reconnect (changed); ansible-timesync inventory/playbook files and working ansible binary confirmed intact post-restart

evidence.requirement: cluster remained healthy across sequential restarts
evidence.summary: After all three restarts completed, final check shows node1 chrony still active/serving and node2 chrony still active and tracking node1 (0A647B0A) as source
